Cryogenic fuels offer an opportunity to diversify aviation fuel carriers using domestic energy sources, relevant for both energy security and resilience. This means cryogenic fuels are a longer-term solution for aircraft but are worth exploring for potential future cost savings, emissions benefits, and energy resilience. Jet X refers to non-drop-in liquid hydrocarbon fuels in the early stages of investigation seeking favorable properties. There are substantial barriers to non-drop-in liquid aviation fuels that are not compatible with existing aircraft and fuel infrastructure, and there is no standardization of Jet X at this time. The inputs needed to produce these energy carriers include biomass, electricity, natural gas, and petroleum. All inputs have multiple uses, creating competition among the various users. Biomass used to produce SAF is also used to produce renewable diesel, biodiesel, ethanol, renewable natural gas, and other biofuels, biochemicals, and bioenergy products. Electricity has a myriad of uses. Additional electrical generation capacity is expected to support growth in data centers supporting artificial intelligence, electric vehicles, and advanced air mobility. LH and PtL could 2 diversify the user base of electricity producers or find rising costs and competition with other uses. LNG and LE will compete with other natural gas applications including heat, electricity generation, chemicals, and other products. Policies shape energy and transportation markets impacting supply, demand, prices, and availability of fuels. They influence how biomass, electricity, natural gas, and petroleum are used, and various policies can shift production toward certain fuels while creating competition among end users. For example, SAF competes with biodiesel and renewable diesel for the same feedstocks. Motivations for transportation fuel policies include diversifying fuel supply to improve energy security and resilience and reducing emissions. Policies can differ in their approach; for example, the U.S. Renewable Fuel Standard provides flexibility in how obligations are met, whereas ReFuelEU requires specific SAF use. Production incentives for SAF and other transportation fuels are typically short-term and frequently expire or change, creating uncertainty that impacts investment in building plants and producers’ decision on fuel production and expansion. v This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. Jet A represents the baseline for comparison of the other aviation energy carriers. Biomass-based SAF is the only commercially available alternative aviation fuel; therefore, there are existing data on current production, consumption, and pricing. LH , LNG, and LE pricing and production 2 are based on uses in non-aviation markets. Table ES-1 provides general information on these various energy carriers for general comparisons.
